ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a quarter-circle region, whose boundary consists of one horizontal straight side, one vertical straight side, and one arc; circle K is inside this region, and is tangent to both mutually perpendicular straight sides and the outer arc. Reasoning: Let the center of the quarter circle be the intersection of the two straight sides, and the radius be 6. Taking the two straight sides as coordinate axes, the outer arc satisfies x^2+y^2=6^2. Let the radius of circle K be r. Because circle K is tangent to both perpendicular straight sides, the distances from the center of circle K to the two straight sides are both r, so the center coordinates can be taken as (r,r). Circle K is internally tangent to the quarter-circle arc with radius 6, so the distance between the two centers equals 6-r. The distance between the two centers is sqrt(r^2+r^2)=r sqrt(2), therefore r sqrt(2)=6-r. Solving gives r(sqrt(2)+1)=6, so r=6/(sqrt(2)+1)=6(sqrt(2)-1).

method.method_draft: Set up coordinates from the diagram: take the corner where the horizontal and vertical sides meet as the center of the quarter circle, with the two straight sides as coordinate axes and the quarter-circle arc given by x^2+y^2=6^2 in the sector. From the image, circle K is tangent to both perpendicular straight sides, so if its radius is r, its center must be at distance r from each side, e.g. at (r,r). Because K is also internally tangent to the quarter-circle arc, the distance between the two circle centers equals 6-r. Compute the center distance as sqrt(r^2+r^2)=r sqrt(2), then solve r sqrt(2)=6-r to get r=6/(sqrt(2)+1)=6(sqrt(2)-1).

method.method_draft: Use a synthetic center-line argument. From the figure, the center O of the quarter circle is the corner where the horizontal and vertical radii meet. Since circle K touches both perpendicular sides, its center C lies on the 45-degree angle bisector of the corner. Drop perpendiculars from C to the two sides; both have length r, the radius of K, forming an isosceles right triangle with hypotenuse OC=r sqrt(2). The point where K touches the outer arc lies on the same line OC, because tangent circles have collinear centers at their tangency point. Along this diagonal radius of the quarter circle, the total length from O to the outer arc is 6, split as OC plus the small radius r. Thus r sqrt(2)+r=6, so r=6/(sqrt(2)+1)=6(sqrt(2)-1).

推理：设四分之一圆的圆心为 O，即两条互相垂直的半径相交的角点；设圆 K 的圆心为 C，半径为 r。因为圆 K 同时与两条互相垂直的边相切，所以 C 到两条边的距离都等于 r，因此 C 在这个直角的 45° 角平分线上。于是从 C 向两边作垂线，可以得到一个等腰直角三角形，直角边都是 r，所以 OC = r√2。又因为圆 K 与外侧四分之一圆弧相切，切点在两圆圆心连线上；四分之一圆半径为 6，所以沿着 OC 方向，从 O 到外弧的长度为 6，且它被分成 OC 和圆 K 的半径 r。因此 r√2 + r = 6。解得 r(√2 + 1) = 6，所以 r = 6/(√2 + 1) = 6(√2 - 1)。
